commit 3de619f50c57c3bde8105a3d998f408d8b40abad
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 08:23:02 +0000

    R5 governor: overspeed limit for momentum entries and ranked FSRN
    
    Under full authority the governor admitted 0 of 3559 real candidates (block 1,
    trial 0). Two scale mismatches caused it:
    
    - The z comparator was a mean-reversion gate (BUY only when price is >= 1.9
      sigma below its mean) while PA candidates follow momentum. The governor now
      takes an entry_mode; the replay engine uses trend_overspeed, which admits
      unless the side-signed z exceeds -base_z + feedback offset - grid droop.
      Poor realized R and an adverse grid lower that limit, as they lower
      dynamic_z. mean_reversion remains the default for the native plant.
    - FSRN compared raw PA/studies confidence (candidates pass at >= 0.15,
      typically 0.15-0.4) with a 0.60 hurdle. FSRN is now the side-aligned min of
      each measure's causal percentile rank over gov_z_window_bars, so the hurdle
      means "top 40% of recent conviction". ID confidence (identical to PA
      confidence) is dropped. No registry change.
    
    Adds a regression test that a full-authority replay with the real decision
    path admits momentum candidates.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 6ab7606d2d6e3dcacf3582789c56bdc1b95a7ed2
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-15 01:31:10 +0000

    Wire the native R5 five-bay plant into the PAPER_APPLY trading loop
    
    In PAPER_APPLY the orchestrator now drives CentralPlantMasterDCS directly:
    
    - Every bar: plant.step_bar() applies an R5 dynamic environment (bay
      governor/AVR/relay gains), steps the HRSG thermal cycle from GTG mass
      flow (volume ratio) x exhaust temperature (range/ATR), and rebalances
      capital so low steam pressure derates CSTG1/CSTG2/BPSTG. The snapshot's
      per-bay gain schedule scales the MPC entry/exit PIDs and the continuous
      exit PID.
    - Entry: evaluate_entry() gates every candidate (side-aware,
      trend_overspeed comparator); quantity = min(quantity, AVR lot capped by
      bay HRSG headroom x governor FSR).
    - Fill: on_trade_filled() consumes the Engine-A latch and binds the trade
      to its bay with its own governor inner loop; release_position() on close.
    - Positions: evaluate_position_control() every bar; substation/SEL/AVR
      trips, Engine-A 15:15 square-off and HRSG pressure collapse arm an exit
      at the next open as plant_trip:<reason>.
    
    Also fixes EngineStateStore(":memory:"), which opened a new empty database
    per connection so the Engine-A latch table never existed.
    
    scripts/r5_plant_wiring_probe.py runs the instrumented 100-bar replay.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UE4gousSZRwX4exwc8jWxK

    docs(r5): black-box audit of the sealed V2 engine, with code evidence and a fix order
    
    Walks PA, chart studies, ID, MPC/PID, governor entry and position control, exit
    PID, sizing, risk/pre-submit gates and costs. Main findings: PA sums
    non-directional inputs into the signed signal; six confidence thresholds, of
    which the calibrated one never binds; exits decided by a ~uniform percentile-rank
    conviction gate that ignores minimum hold; PID outputs clamped, advisory or used
    as on/off triggers; Gate12 rejects ~1/3 of valid candidates by float rounding at
    rr == 1.5; HMM fed a gappy series; 1-minute-ATR stops make costs ~0.5R.
    
    The ID research hook now also records PA's four components and whether the
    directional terms alone give the same side, to test the PA-1 hypothesis on blade.

    diag(r5): adverse-tail ladder, trades vs controls
    
    The corrected Stage-A run shows a fatter favourable tail for the trades than
    for their controls (>=1R: 31% vs 23% at 15 bars). That is direction only if
    the adverse tail is not equally fatter; if both tails are, the entries select

commit 2eeccdf9bfaee0954181486ea373c1da9f3c23aa
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 13:02:48 +0000

    diag(r5): break-even sweep on synthesized fills; first-fill hold-to-close competitor
    
    - The friction sweep no longer re-uses recorded fills. Pre-slippage market
      prices are recovered once with the sealed 5 bps; at each of 0/1/2/3/4/5 bps
      per leg new fills are synthesized and brokerage, exchange charges and STT are
      recomputed on them with the engine's formula. At 5 bps this reproduces the
      engine's fills, charges and net (tested); net is monotone in slippage.
    - Competitor priced on the same entries at every slippage: only the first
      executed entry per symbol and session, held to the session close. It is a
      lower bound on a first-raw-signal/EOD strategy, since it still waits for the

commit 87c0a8999c57a5e27d230b4eb411124667ad7a5b
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:41:29 +0000

    diag(r5): fix look-ahead in time-matched controls (use other sessions)
    
    The +/-30-bar same-session control window (cbfdaca) included the bars just
    before the entry. Every R5 entry follows a 0.6-2.5R run in its own direction,
    so controls placed there rode the move that triggered the entry: on the V2
    Stage-A run the control mean jumped to +0.45R at 15 bars (82% positive) and
    the reported entry "edge" to -0.36R. That was a biased null, not a finding.
    
    Controls are now drawn from the block's OTHER sessions: same symbol, side and
    risk unit, within +/-30 minutes of the trade's time of day, entered at the bar
    close, full horizon where that session allows (the session-close horizon runs
    to each control's own close). With no other session there is no control and
    the trade is excluded from the edge statistics. Regression test: a run before
    the entry on the same day must not appear in the controls.

commit f53c7f529af6a94fa75452afa72d742b4191254d
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:15:35 +0000

    diag(r5): measure the output as an exposure pulse train
    
    The whole R5 stack emits one thing per symbol: an exposure pulse (leading edge
    = entry and polarity, width = bars held, trailing edge = exit, off-interval =
    gap to the next pulse on the same symbol and session). Each pulse pays a
    switching loss (round-trip friction, R) and captures an energy (pre-slippage
    market move, R); energy - loss = net.
    
    Reported per source and pooled: pulse count, SELL share, width median/IQR and
    share <= 3 bars, pulses per active symbol-session, off-interval median and
    share <= 5/15 min, polarity flips within a session, and energy vs switching
    loss by width bucket (1-3, 4-10, 11-30, 31+ bars) -- the data needed to set a
    minimum on-time, a refractory period and a repetition limit.

commit cbfdaca83ece6854e570c94672ba02102779943f
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    diag(r5): exit-independent MFE ladders, time-matched controls, EOD horizon
    
    Review follow-ups:
    - Fixed-horizon MFE ladders (1/5/15/30/60 bars and the session close) per
      trade, whatever V2 actually did, so an entry cut early by FSRN is still
      measured on its full forward opportunity. Each rung is shown against the
      same ladder for the matched controls: a random walk's running maximum grows
      like sqrt(h), so a fixed-horizon ladder alone would suggest opportunity
      where there is none (verified on a synthetic random walk: trades ~ controls).
    - Controls are time-matched: random bars within +/-30 bars of the trade's time
      of day, same session, symbol, side and risk unit, full horizon where the
      session allows.

      and vs the next bar's open), so the control entry reference is checked, not
      assumed. The V2 Stage-A run already measured fill ~ entry-bar close
      (+0.006R, CI -0.010..+0.025).
    - New horizons 60 bars and session close.

commit e1cfc63b9e3367cd180f2991ece7f8192afdac53
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 11:02:26 +0000

    diag(r5): exit-authority regret, MFE ladder and FSR channel attribution
    
    - FSR exits are attributed to their controlling channel (FSRN, FSRT, FSRA,
      FSRS, FSRM), parsed from the engine's FSR_BELOW_EXIT:<channel> reason.
    - Exit regret per exit reason: close, best and worst move over the 1/3/5/10
      bars after the exit bar, from the pre-slippage exit price, capped at the
      session. Positive close/best = exited too early.
    - MFE ladder: share of trades whose in-trade MFE reached 0.10/0.30/0.50/1.00R,
      both on the engine's recorded basis (from the fill, after entry slippage)
      and from the pre-slippage market entry, so slippage is not read as an
      entry that never moved.

       supersedes, a dirty tree, or an engine commit that is not HEAD.

       SHA, stage, params, block sessions); ledgers hash in the worker's JSON form.
       No bridge.json is written on V2_REFERENCE_MISMATCH, LEGACY_SHADOW_MISMATCH or

commit 7ded8417074b828312eeb77210826ecc0cd6a07d
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-29 04:58:00 +0000

    R5 diagnostics: governor trace tool for bay-restricted Stage A blocks
    
    scripts/r5_governor_trace.py reuses the Step 5 worker's sealed block loader and
    builds the engine as execute_block does, restricted to one bay's canonical
    symbols. Pass-through wrappers record the gain schedule (begin_bar environment,
    apply_runtime_profile), the outer realized-R PID, the entry comparator
    (dynamic_z, droop, overspeed limit), the inner per-position PID, the Mark V
    limiter, and bay protection and admission. --verify-passthrough reruns
    uninstrumented and requires an identical trade list. No engine, protocol,
    registry or Stage A state is modified.

commit c0b4672fa45498d628f1646d60c75fd206803755
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 10:54:25 +0000

    R5 governor: noise-scaled path-error tolerance (gov_path_error_sigma)
    
    Trial 0 under full authority (146 trades, PF 0.15) attributed the loss to
    GOVERNOR_PATH_ERROR: 82 exits, net -12.4k, PF 0.01, almost all within 1-3
    bars, while trades held 6-20 bars were profitable before costs. The inner
    loop exited once the trade lagged its reference path by max(|target_r|,
    |dynamic_offset_max|) = 0.30R -- the outer loop's realized-R setpoint reused
    as a tracking tolerance. One 1-minute bar moves ~0.8R (1R = 1.2 ATR), so that
    fired on noise.
    
    The tolerance is now gov_path_error_sigma * (ATR / initial risk) *
    sqrt(elapsed bars): the lag must exceed the market's own noise envelope.
    New registry parameter gov_path_error_sigma (EXTERNAL-only, calibratable,
    default 2.0 in [1.0, 3.5]); 170 targets / 122 eligible; new frozen identity.
    Without the noise inputs the governor keeps the legacy tolerance (native plant
    unchanged); the replay's position decision fails closed if ATR is unavailable.
    
    r5_loss_attribution.py also reads Step 5 candidate output (per-block trades).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 3de619f50c57c3bde8105a3d998f408d8b40abad
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 08:23:02 +0000

    R5 governor: overspeed limit for momentum entries and ranked FSRN
    
    Under full authority the governor admitted 0 of 3559 real candidates (block 1,
    trial 0). Two scale mismatches caused it:
    
    - The z comparator was a mean-reversion gate (BUY only when price is >= 1.9
      sigma below its mean) while PA candidates follow momentum. The governor now
      takes an entry_mode; the replay engine uses trend_overspeed, which admits
      unless the side-signed z exceeds -base_z + feedback offset - grid droop.
      Poor realized R and an adverse grid lower that limit, as they lower
      dynamic_z. mean_reversion remains the default for the native plant.
    - FSRN compared raw PA/studies confidence (candidates pass at >= 0.15,
      typically 0.15-0.4) with a 0.60 hurdle. FSRN is now the side-aligned min of
      each measure's causal percentile rank over gov_z_window_bars, so the hurdle
      means "top 40% of recent conviction". ID confidence (identical to PA
      confidence) is dropped. No registry change.
    
    Adds a regression test that a full-authority replay with the real decision
    path admits momentum candidates.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 30c3fb5eff5139b3e746f6ce69bd18e260767d2f
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-27 14:23:26 +0000

    R5: governor entry/exit authority, Mark V gate, MiCOM protection, audit tools
    
    Governor authority (H1)
    - revision5/governor_authority.py: causal market telemetry (z-score, ATR,
      vibration, velocity, bay exhaust spread) and a Mark V minimum value gate
      (FSRN/FSRT/FSRA/FSRS/FSRM) with fail-closed input validation.
    - BayTurbineClosedLoopGovernor: per-position inner loop keyed by trade id
      (no inherited ratchet) and side-symmetric entry comparator.
    - Orchestrator governor_authority = advisory (default) | full. In full mode
      the governor is the only entry and discretionary-exit authority: it
      decides every candidate, derates size by FSR, arms exits for the next
      bar's open and ratchets the protective stop one way. Safety and
      protection still outrank it; the exit PID saturation, HMM regime and
      path-loop exits become advisory events.
    - scripts/run_r5_paper_replay.py: --governor-authority (default full).
    
    MiCOM protection
    - Relay evaluated every portfolio timestamp in PAPER_APPLY from the causal
      NIFTY 15-minute grid and the daily fleet MTM drawdown. A trip opens the
      intertie and unwinds open positions; MiCOM recloses what it opened. The
      ANSI 67 latch resets at the session boundary.
    
    Registry
    - 17 governor-authority / MiCOM values (13 calibratable offline, 4 fixed).
      New frozen identity; the sealed calibration protocol must be re-sealed.
    
    Tools
    - scripts/r5_parameter_inventory.py -> docs/R5_PARAMETER_INVENTORY.md:
      classified registry parameters and every unowned engine literal.
    - scripts/r5_loss_attribution.py: gross vs costs, exit reason, bay, side,
      hour, holding period and excursion breakdown of a replay report.
    - docs/R5_GOVERNOR_AUTHORITY.md: authority matrix, wiring and open items.

commit 6ab7606d2d6e3dcacf3582789c56bdc1b95a7ed2
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-15 01:31:10 +0000

    Wire the native R5 five-bay plant into the PAPER_APPLY trading loop
    
    In PAPER_APPLY the orchestrator now drives CentralPlantMasterDCS directly:
    
    - Every bar: plant.step_bar() applies an R5 dynamic environment (bay
      governor/AVR/relay gains), steps the HRSG thermal cycle from GTG mass
      flow (volume ratio) x exhaust temperature (range/ATR), and rebalances
      capital so low steam pressure derates CSTG1/CSTG2/BPSTG. The snapshot's
      per-bay gain schedule scales the MPC entry/exit PIDs and the continuous
      exit PID.
    - Entry: evaluate_entry() gates every candidate (side-aware,
      trend_overspeed comparator); quantity = min(quantity, AVR lot capped by
      bay HRSG headroom x governor FSR).
    - Fill: on_trade_filled() consumes the Engine-A latch and binds the trade
      to its bay with its own governor inner loop; release_position() on close.
    - Positions: evaluate_position_control() every bar; substation/SEL/AVR
      trips, Engine-A 15:15 square-off and HRSG pressure collapse arm an exit
      at the next open as plant_trip:<reason>.
    
    Also fixes EngineStateStore(":memory:"), which opened a new empty database
    per connection so the Engine-A latch table never existed.
    
    scripts/r5_plant_wiring_probe.py runs the instrumented 100-bar replay.

    docs(r5): black-box audit of the sealed V2 engine, with code evidence and a fix order
    
    Walks PA, chart studies, ID, MPC/PID, governor entry and position control, exit
    PID, sizing, risk/pre-submit gates and costs. Main findings: PA sums
    non-directional inputs into the signed signal; six confidence thresholds, of
    which the calibrated one never binds; exits decided by a ~uniform percentile-rank
    conviction gate that ignores minimum hold; PID outputs clamped, advisory or used
    as on/off triggers; Gate12 rejects ~1/3 of valid candidates by float rounding at
    rr == 1.5; HMM fed a gappy series; 1-minute-ATR stops make costs ~0.5R.
    
    The ID research hook now also records PA's four components and whether the
    directional terms alone give the same side, to test the PA-1 hypothesis on blade.

    diag(r5): adverse-tail ladder, trades vs controls
    
    The corrected Stage-A run shows a fatter favourable tail for the trades than
    for their controls (>=1R: 31% vs 23% at 15 bars). That is direction only if
    the adverse tail is not equally fatter; if both tails are, the entries select
    volatility (bigger moves either way), which direction-based selectivity cannot
    exploit. The report now prints the fixed-horizon adverse ladder (<=-0.10/0.30/

commit 2eeccdf9bfaee0954181486ea373c1da9f3c23aa
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 13:02:48 +0000

    diag(r5): break-even sweep on synthesized fills; first-fill hold-to-close competitor
    
    - The friction sweep no longer re-uses recorded fills. Pre-slippage market
      prices are recovered once with the sealed 5 bps; at each of 0/1/2/3/4/5 bps
      per leg new fills are synthesized and brokerage, exchange charges and STT are
      recomputed on them with the engine's formula. At 5 bps this reproduces the
      engine's fills, charges and net (tested); net is monotone in slippage.
    - Competitor priced on the same entries at every slippage: only the first
      executed entry per symbol and session, held to the session close. It is a
      lower bound on a first-raw-signal/EOD strategy, since it still waits for the
      full entry stack.

commit 87c0a8999c57a5e27d230b4eb411124667ad7a5b
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:41:29 +0000

    diag(r5): fix look-ahead in time-matched controls (use other sessions)
    
    The +/-30-bar same-session control window (cbfdaca) included the bars just
    before the entry. Every R5 entry follows a 0.6-2.5R run in its own direction,
    so controls placed there rode the move that triggered the entry: on the V2
    Stage-A run the control mean jumped to +0.45R at 15 bars (82% positive) and
    the reported entry "edge" to -0.36R. That was a biased null, not a finding.
    
    Controls are now drawn from the block's OTHER sessions: same symbol, side and
    risk unit, within +/-30 minutes of the trade's time of day, entered at the bar
    close, full horizon where that session allows (the session-close horizon runs
    to each control's own close). With no other session there is no control and
    the trade is excluded from the edge statistics. Regression test: a run before
    the entry on the same day must not appear in the controls.

commit f53c7f529af6a94fa75452afa72d742b4191254d
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:15:35 +0000

    diag(r5): measure the output as an exposure pulse train
    
    The whole R5 stack emits one thing per symbol: an exposure pulse (leading edge
    = entry and polarity, width = bars held, trailing edge = exit, off-interval =
    gap to the next pulse on the same symbol and session). Each pulse pays a
    switching loss (round-trip friction, R) and captures an energy (pre-slippage
    market move, R); energy - loss = net.
    
    Reported per source and pooled: pulse count, SELL share, width median/IQR and
    share <= 3 bars, pulses per active symbol-session, off-interval median and
    share <= 5/15 min, polarity flips within a session, and energy vs switching
    loss by width bucket (1-3, 4-10, 11-30, 31+ bars) -- the data needed to set a
    minimum on-time, a refractory period and a repetition limit.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit cbfdaca83ece6854e570c94672ba02102779943f
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    diag(r5): exit-independent MFE ladders, time-matched controls, EOD horizon
    
    Review follow-ups:
    - Fixed-horizon MFE ladders (1/5/15/30/60 bars and the session close) per
      trade, whatever V2 actually did, so an entry cut early by FSRN is still
      measured on its full forward opportunity. Each rung is shown against the
      same ladder for the matched controls: a random walk's running maximum grows
      like sqrt(h), so a fixed-horizon ladder alone would suggest opportunity
      where there is none (verified on a synthetic random walk: trades ~ controls).
    - Controls are time-matched: random bars within +/-30 bars of the trade's time
      of day, same session, symbol, side and risk unit, full horizon where the
      session allows.

      and vs the next bar's open), so the control entry reference is checked, not
      assumed. The V2 Stage-A run already measured fill ~ entry-bar close
      (+0.006R, CI -0.010..+0.025).
    - New horizons 60 bars and session close.

commit e1cfc63b9e3367cd180f2991ece7f8192afdac53
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 11:02:26 +0000

    diag(r5): exit-authority regret, MFE ladder and FSR channel attribution
    
    - FSR exits are attributed to their controlling channel (FSRN, FSRT, FSRA,
      FSRS, FSRM), parsed from the engine's FSR_BELOW_EXIT:<channel> reason.
    - Exit regret per exit reason: close, best and worst move over the 1/3/5/10
      bars after the exit bar, from the pre-slippage exit price, capped at the
      session. Positive close/best = exited too early.
    - MFE ladder: share of trades whose in-trade MFE reached 0.10/0.30/0.50/1.00R,
      both on the engine's recorded basis (from the fill, after entry slippage)
      and from the pre-slippage market entry, so slippage is not read as an
      entry that never moved.

commit c0b4672fa45498d628f1646d60c75fd206803755
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 10:54:25 +0000

    R5 governor: noise-scaled path-error tolerance (gov_path_error_sigma)
    
    Trial 0 under full authority (146 trades, PF 0.15) attributed the loss to
    GOVERNOR_PATH_ERROR: 82 exits, net -12.4k, PF 0.01, almost all within 1-3
    bars, while trades held 6-20 bars were profitable before costs. The inner
    loop exited once the trade lagged its reference path by max(|target_r|,
    |dynamic_offset_max|) = 0.30R -- the outer loop's realized-R setpoint reused
    as a tracking tolerance. One 1-minute bar moves ~0.8R (1R = 1.2 ATR), so that
    fired on noise.
    
    The tolerance is now gov_path_error_sigma * (ATR / initial risk) *
    sqrt(elapsed bars): the lag must exceed the market's own noise envelope.
    New registry parameter gov_path_error_sigma (EXTERNAL-only, calibratable,
    default 2.0 in [1.0, 3.5]); 170 targets / 122 eligible; new frozen identity.
    Without the noise inputs the governor keeps the legacy tolerance (native plant
    unchanged); the replay's position decision fails closed if ATR is unavailable.
    
    r5_loss_attribution.py also reads Step 5 candidate output (per-block trades).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 3de619f50c57c3bde8105a3d998f408d8b40abad
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 08:23:02 +0000

    R5 governor: overspeed limit for momentum entries and ranked FSRN
    
    Under full authority the governor admitted 0 of 3559 real candidates (block 1,
    trial 0). Two scale mismatches caused it:
    
    - The z comparator was a mean-reversion gate (BUY only when price is >= 1.9
      sigma below its mean) while PA candidates follow momentum. The governor now
      takes an entry_mode; the replay engine uses trend_overspeed, which admits
      unless the side-signed z exceeds -base_z + feedback offset - grid droop.
      Poor realized R and an adverse grid lower that limit, as they lower
      dynamic_z. mean_reversion remains the default for the native plant.
    - FSRN compared raw PA/studies confidence (candidates pass at >= 0.15,
      typically 0.15-0.4) with a 0.60 hurdle. FSRN is now the side-aligned min of
      each measure's causal percentile rank over gov_z_window_bars, so the hurdle
      means "top 40% of recent conviction". ID confidence (identical to PA
      confidence) is dropped. No registry change.
    
    Adds a regression test that a full-authority replay with the real decision
    path admits momentum candidates.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 30c3fb5eff5139b3e746f6ce69bd18e260767d2f
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-27 14:23:26 +0000

    R5: governor entry/exit authority, Mark V gate, MiCOM protection, audit tools
    
    Governor authority (H1)
    - revision5/governor_authority.py: causal market telemetry (z-score, ATR,
      vibration, velocity, bay exhaust spread) and a Mark V minimum value gate
      (FSRN/FSRT/FSRA/FSRS/FSRM) with fail-closed input validation.
    - BayTurbineClosedLoopGovernor: per-position inner loop keyed by trade id
      (no inherited ratchet) and side-symmetric entry comparator.
    - Orchestrator governor_authority = advisory (default) | full. In full mode
      the governor is the only entry and discretionary-exit authority: it
      decides every candidate, derates size by FSR, arms exits for the next
      bar's open and ratchets the protective stop one way. Safety and
      protection still outrank it; the exit PID saturation, HMM regime and
      path-loop exits become advisory events.
    - scripts/run_r5_paper_replay.py: --governor-authority (default full).
    
    MiCOM protection
    - Relay evaluated every portfolio timestamp in PAPER_APPLY from the causal
      NIFTY 15-minute grid and the daily fleet MTM drawdown. A trip opens the
      intertie and unwinds open positions; MiCOM recloses what it opened. The
      ANSI 67 latch resets at the session boundary.

        fallback is removed.  An invalid replay timestamp now stops the run.

        tz-aware timestamps on the exchange (Asia/Kolkata) clock.
    H5  _execute_exit updates the authoritative books (completed trades, symbol
        lockouts, equity, open_trades, exit state, MTM) before realized-R feedback
        and research telemetry, so a later defect can no longer leave a flat broker
        position recorded as open.  bars_held is never fabricated; without exit
        controller state the expectancy outcome is recorded as unavailable.
        CausalEntryExpectancyLedger.record_outcome validates the full outcome
        before consuming the pending candidate.

commit be053d4853fd74647151513d5e61ce508a3fdbc8
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-20 10:40:03 +0000

    fix: Resolve 3 critical capital-bleed production issues
    
    ISSUE #1: Position Quantity Default Too Restrictive
    - Gate09 defaults to 1 share for unlisted symbols
    - Changed: .get(symbol, 1) → .get(symbol, 100)
    - Impact: 45 symbols were stuck at 1 share, now can scale to 100
    
    ISSUE #2: Slippage Gate Choking on Sub-Tick Noise
    - SLIPPAGE_REJECT_THRESHOLD_PERCENT = 0.10% rejects normal tick noise
    - Changed: 0.10% → 0.35% (ignores sub-tick ₹0.50-1.00 on INFY)
    - Impact: Legitimate entries no longer blocked by noise
    
    ISSUE #3: Re-Entry Protection Too Lenient
    - CONSECUTIVE_LOSSES_THRESHOLD = 5 allows 4 losing trades before halt
    - Changed: 5 → 2 (block re-entry after 2nd consecutive loss)
    - Impact: Stops compounding losses immediately
    
    These 3 operational fixes stop capital bleed in production trading.
    All tests validate correctly with new thresholds.

    - New: rolling_setpoint_provider.py (140 lines, unified baseline computation)
    - Problem: Entry and exit PIDs computed baselines differently (asymmetric control)
    - Solution: Single RollingSetpointProvider prevents circular dependency
    - Test: 6/6 tests passing (rolling means, no look-ahead bias, multi-symbol support)
    
    CRITICAL FIX #2: Dead Code Removal
    - Deleted: master_control_system.py (467 lines of incomplete, unused code)
    - Problem: Module explicitly marked "Known Incomplete", never instantiated
    - Verification: Zero external references confirmed via grep
    - Impact: Cleaner codebase, eliminated confusion about active systems
    
    CRITICAL FIX #3: Integral Anti-Windup Implementation
    - New: bounded_pid_controller.py (250 lines, proper anti-windup)
    - Problem: simple-pid clamps OUTPUT (wrong) instead of integral (correct)
    - Solution: Clamp integral term only → allows proportional/derivative recovery
    - Test: 6/6 tests passing (integral clamping, recovery, calibrated gains)
    - Benefit: Prevents saturation under sustained error, enables proper response
    
    CRITICAL FIX #4: HMM Valid State Mask Logic
    - New: regime_hmm_fixed.py (260 lines, dual-threshold state validity)
    - Problem: HMM only checks fractional occupancy (5%) → 10-sample states marked valid
    - Solution: Dual thresholds (occupancy 5% AND absolute sample count ≥20)
    - Test: 6/6 tests passing (insufficient samples rejected, parameter validation)
    - Benefit: Prevents false positive stress detection from noise-driven state splits

commit 4d90b5717f74a505847e7f1610e835ca180fec62

    Add Engine C: R5 CCPP engine executed natively by Backtrader
    
    engine_c/ drives the shared R5 decision code from completed Backtrader bars
    and sends approved intents as native Backtrader market orders to BackBroker.
    Fills happen at the next bar's open with independent NSE commission and
    slippage configuration. R5 books positions only from Backtrader execution
    bits. Native partial (FixedBarPerc), cancel, margin and venue-rule reject
    paths are handled. Working entries reserve concurrency, gross, sector and
    bay capacity. A FillLedger/Reconciler compares Backtrader accounting with
    the R5 fill-derived and trade ledgers after every event, every tick and at
    completion, and fails closed on a break.
    
    Adds the historical-data contract (manifest verification, raw-row audit),
    the CLI runner, an Engine A reference runner, a read-only three-engine
    comparison tool, a dependency manifest and 19 tests. Engine A and Engine B
    code, golden masters and data are unchanged. Offline backtest only.

commit 6ab7606d2d6e3dcacf3582789c56bdc1b95a7ed2
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-15 01:31:10 +0000

    Wire the native R5 five-bay plant into the PAPER_APPLY trading loop
    
    In PAPER_APPLY the orchestrator now drives CentralPlantMasterDCS directly:
    
    - Every bar: plant.step_bar() applies an R5 dynamic environment (bay
      governor/AVR/relay gains), steps the HRSG thermal cycle from GTG mass
      flow (volume ratio) x exhaust temperature (range/ATR), and rebalances
      capital so low steam pressure derates CSTG1/CSTG2/BPSTG. The snapshot's
      per-bay gain schedule scales the MPC entry/exit PIDs and the continuous
      exit PID.
    - Entry: evaluate_entry() gates every candidate (side-aware,
      trend_overspeed comparator); quantity = min(quantity, AVR lot capped by
      bay HRSG headroom x governor FSR).
    - Fill: on_trade_filled() consumes the Engine-A latch and binds the trade
      to its bay with its own governor inner loop; release_position() on close.
    - Positions: evaluate_position_control() every bar; substation/SEL/AVR
      trips, Engine-A 15:15 square-off and HRSG pressure collapse arm an exit
      at the next open as plant_trip:<reason>.
    
    Also fixes EngineStateStore(":memory:"), which opened a new empty database
    per connection so the Engine-A latch table never existed.
    
    scripts/r5_plant_wiring_probe.py runs the instrumented 100-bar replay.

commit 86a7fcaa433aa066eae08d3b342661d35bd50028
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-01 02:24:11 +0000

    docs(r5): black-box audit of the sealed V2 engine, with code evidence and a fix order
    
    Walks PA, chart studies, ID, MPC/PID, governor entry and position control, exit
    PID, sizing, risk/pre-submit gates and costs. Main findings: PA sums
    non-directional inputs into the signed signal; six confidence thresholds, of
    which the calibrated one never binds; exits decided by a ~uniform percentile-rank
    conviction gate that ignores minimum hold; PID outputs clamped, advisory or used
    as on/off triggers; Gate12 rejects ~1/3 of valid candidates by float rounding at
    rr == 1.5; HMM fed a gappy series; 1-minute-ATR stops make costs ~0.5R.
    
    The ID research hook now also records PA's four components and whether the
    directional terms alone give the same side, to test the PA-1 hypothesis on blade.

commit 87c0a8999c57a5e27d230b4eb411124667ad7a5b
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:41:29 +0000

    diag(r5): fix look-ahead in time-matched controls (use other sessions)
    
    The +/-30-bar same-session control window (cbfdaca) included the bars just
    before the entry. Every R5 entry follows a 0.6-2.5R run in its own direction,
    so controls placed there rode the move that triggered the entry: on the V2
    Stage-A run the control mean jumped to +0.45R at 15 bars (82% positive) and
    the reported entry "edge" to -0.36R. That was a biased null, not a finding.
    
    Controls are now drawn from the block's OTHER sessions: same symbol, side and
    risk unit, within +/-30 minutes of the trade's time of day, entered at the bar
    close, full horizon where that session allows (the session-close horizon runs
    to each control's own close). With no other session there is no control and
    the trade is excluded from the edge statistics. Regression test: a run before
    the entry on the same day must not appear in the controls.

commit f53c7f529af6a94fa75452afa72d742b4191254d
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:15:35 +0000

    diag(r5): measure the output as an exposure pulse train
    
    The whole R5 stack emits one thing per symbol: an exposure pulse (leading edge
    = entry and polarity, width = bars held, trailing edge = exit, off-interval =
    gap to the next pulse on the same symbol and session). Each pulse pays a
    switching loss (round-trip friction, R) and captures an energy (pre-slippage
    market move, R); energy - loss = net.
    
    Reported per source and pooled: pulse count, SELL share, width median/IQR and
    share <= 3 bars, pulses per active symbol-session, off-interval median and
    share <= 5/15 min, polarity flips within a session, and energy vs switching
    loss by width bucket (1-3, 4-10, 11-30, 31+ bars) -- the data needed to set a
    minimum on-time, a refractory period and a repetition limit.

commit 7ded8417074b828312eeb77210826ecc0cd6a07d
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-29 04:58:00 +0000

    R5 diagnostics: governor trace tool for bay-restricted Stage A blocks
    
    scripts/r5_governor_trace.py reuses the Step 5 worker's sealed block loader and
    builds the engine as execute_block does, restricted to one bay's canonical
    symbols. Pass-through wrappers record the gain schedule (begin_bar environment,
    apply_runtime_profile), the outer realized-R PID, the entry comparator
    (dynamic_z, droop, overspeed limit), the inner per-position PID, the Mark V
    limiter, and bay protection and admission. --verify-passthrough reruns
    uninstrumented and requires an identical trade list. No engine, protocol,
    registry or Stage A state is modified.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit c0b4672fa45498d628f1646d60c75fd206803755
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 10:54:25 +0000

    R5 governor: noise-scaled path-error tolerance (gov_path_error_sigma)
    
    Trial 0 under full authority (146 trades, PF 0.15) attributed the loss to
    GOVERNOR_PATH_ERROR: 82 exits, net -12.4k, PF 0.01, almost all within 1-3
    bars, while trades held 6-20 bars were profitable before costs. The inner
    loop exited once the trade lagged its reference path by max(|target_r|,
    |dynamic_offset_max|) = 0.30R -- the outer loop's realized-R setpoint reused
    as a tracking tolerance. One 1-minute bar moves ~0.8R (1R = 1.2 ATR), so that
    fired on noise.
    
    The tolerance is now gov_path_error_sigma * (ATR / initial risk) *
    sqrt(elapsed bars): the lag must exceed the market's own noise envelope.
    New registry parameter gov_path_error_sigma (EXTERNAL-only, calibratable,
    default 2.0 in [1.0, 3.5]); 170 targets / 122 eligible; new frozen identity.
    Without the noise inputs the governor keeps the legacy tolerance (native plant
    unchanged); the replay's position decision fails closed if ATR is unavailable.
    
    r5_loss_attribution.py also reads Step 5 candidate output (per-block trades).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 3de619f50c57c3bde8105a3d998f408d8b40abad
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 08:23:02 +0000

    R5 governor: overspeed limit for momentum entries and ranked FSRN
    
    Under full authority the governor admitted 0 of 3559 real candidates (block 1,
    trial 0). Two scale mismatches caused it:
    
    - The z comparator was a mean-reversion gate (BUY only when price is >= 1.9
      sigma below its mean) while PA candidates follow momentum. The governor now
      takes an entry_mode; the replay engine uses trend_overspeed, which admits
      unless the side-signed z exceeds -base_z + feedback offset - grid droop.
      Poor realized R and an adverse grid lower that limit, as they lower
      dynamic_z. mean_reversion remains the default for the native plant.
    - FSRN compared raw PA/studies confidence (candidates pass at >= 0.15,
      typically 0.15-0.4) with a 0.60 hurdle. FSRN is now the side-aligned min of
      each measure's causal percentile rank over gov_z_window_bars, so the hurdle
      means "top 40% of recent conviction". ID confidence (identical to PA
      confidence) is dropped. No registry change.
    
    Adds a regression test that a full-authority replay with the real decision
    path admits momentum candidates.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

      ANSI 67 latch resets at the session boundary.

    R5: fix exposure double count, wall-clock and fail-open fallbacks, exit bookkeeping order
    
    H2  ECS plant demand is now a total-loading setpoint (grid, protection, bay
        availability).  Current exposure is enforced once, by the paper admission
        cap (budget * reference - current exposure).  Previously the ECS also
        subtracted exposure headroom, so reachable gross exposure converged to
        ~55% of max_gross_exposure_fraction.  Headroom and the ClosedLoopSupervisor
        new-risk derate are still validated and reported as ECS reasons.
    H3  Pre-submit gates use the replay event time only; the datetime.now()
        fallback is removed.  An invalid replay timestamp now stops the run.
    H4  _in_trading_window fails closed (records TRADING_WINDOW_FAULT) and reads
        tz-aware timestamps on the exchange (Asia/Kolkata) clock.
    H5  _execute_exit updates the authoritative books (completed trades, symbol
        lockouts, equity, open_trades, exit state, MTM) before realized-R feedback
        and research telemetry, so a later defect can no longer leave a flat broker
        position recorded as open.  bars_held is never fabricated; without exit
        controller state the expectancy outcome is recorded as unavailable.
        CausalEntryExpectancyLedger.record_outcome validates the full outcome
        before consuming the pending candidate.
    
    Tests: new tests/test_r5_h1_h5_remediation.py (15 tests; 14 fail on the
    previous code).  Two ECS tests updated to the loading-setpoint contract.

commit 6ab7606d2d6e3dcacf3582789c56bdc1b95a7ed2
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-15 01:31:10 +0000

    Wire the native R5 five-bay plant into the PAPER_APPLY trading loop
    
    In PAPER_APPLY the orchestrator now drives CentralPlantMasterDCS directly:
    
    - Every bar: plant.step_bar() applies an R5 dynamic environment (bay
      governor/AVR/relay gains), steps the HRSG thermal cycle from GTG mass
      flow (volume ratio) x exhaust temperature (range/ATR), and rebalances
      capital so low steam pressure derates CSTG1/CSTG2/BPSTG. The snapshot's
      per-bay gain schedule scales the MPC entry/exit PIDs and the continuous
      exit PID.
    - Entry: evaluate_entry() gates every candidate (side-aware,
      trend_overspeed comparator); quantity = min(quantity, AVR lot capped by
      bay HRSG headroom x governor FSR).
    - Fill: on_trade_filled() consumes the Engine-A latch and binds the trade
      to its bay with its own governor inner loop; release_position() on close.
    - Positions: evaluate_position_control() every bar; substation/SEL/AVR
      trips, Engine-A 15:15 square-off and HRSG pressure collapse arm an exit
      at the next open as plant_trip:<reason>.
    
    Also fixes EngineStateStore(":memory:"), which opened a new empty database
    per connection so the Engine-A latch table never existed.
    
    scripts/r5_plant_wiring_probe.py runs the instrumented 100-bar replay.

commit 86a7fcaa433aa066eae08d3b342661d35bd50028
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-01 02:24:11 +0000

    docs(r5): black-box audit of the sealed V2 engine, with code evidence and a fix order
    
    Walks PA, chart studies, ID, MPC/PID, governor entry and position control, exit
    PID, sizing, risk/pre-submit gates and costs. Main findings: PA sums
    non-directional inputs into the signed signal; six confidence thresholds, of
    which the calibrated one never binds; exits decided by a ~uniform percentile-rank
    conviction gate that ignores minimum hold; PID outputs clamped, advisory or used
    as on/off triggers; Gate12 rejects ~1/3 of valid candidates by float rounding at
    rr == 1.5; HMM fed a gappy series; 1-minute-ATR stops make costs ~0.5R.
    
    The ID research hook now also records PA's four components and whether the
    directional terms alone give the same side, to test the PA-1 hypothesis on blade.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 87c0a8999c57a5e27d230b4eb411124667ad7a5b
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    diag(r5): fix look-ahead in time-matched controls (use other sessions)
    
    The +/-30-bar same-session control window (cbfdaca) included the bars just
    before the entry. Every R5 entry follows a 0.6-2.5R run in its own direction,
    so controls placed there rode the move that triggered the entry: on the V2
    Stage-A run the control mean jumped to +0.45R at 15 bars (82% positive) and
    the reported entry "edge" to -0.36R. That was a biased null, not a finding.
    
    Controls are now drawn from the block's OTHER sessions: same symbol, side and
    risk unit, within +/-30 minutes of the trade's time of day, entered at the bar
    close, full horizon where that session allows (the session-close horizon runs
    to each control's own close). With no other session there is no control and
    the trade is excluded from the edge statistics. Regression test: a run before
    the entry on the same day must not appear in the controls.

commit f53c7f529af6a94fa75452afa72d742b4191254d
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:15:35 +0000

    diag(r5): measure the output as an exposure pulse train
    
    The whole R5 stack emits one thing per symbol: an exposure pulse (leading edge
    = entry and polarity, width = bars held, trailing edge = exit, off-interval =
    gap to the next pulse on the same symbol and session). Each pulse pays a
    switching loss (round-trip friction, R) and captures an energy (pre-slippage
    market move, R); energy - loss = net.
    
    Reported per source and pooled: pulse count, SELL share, width median/IQR and
    share <= 3 bars, pulses per active symbol-session, off-interval median and
    share <= 5/15 min, polarity flips within a session, and energy vs switching
    loss by width bucket (1-3, 4-10, 11-30, 31+ bars) -- the data needed to set a
    minimum on-time, a refractory period and a repetition limit.

commit a695913c37eb05bfc87ab4a8a3f5a12bfac89615
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    feat(engine): Protocol V3 hardened closed-loop position control + shadow exit tracker
    
    Opt-in engine mode governor_position_control="closed_loop_v3" (full authority only;
    "legacy" default is the V2 inner loop, unchanged):
    - two-rate leaky inner integral I = clip(gamma*I + e, +/-I_max), gamma_fast when
      |e| > tau_error_multiplier * ATR/risk, Ki applied once
    - no derivative kick: D = 0 on the first sample and the first trailing-active sample
    - per-bar trailing gap base_gap*(1 - kappa*tanh(u)), floored by one bar of noise and
      minimum_gap; eligible after grace_bars and mfe_activation_r; one-way floor armed
      for the next bar; no binary path-error exit; no order-flow input
    - reference path applies curve_gamma once (expected_r and lower_bound_r)
    
    Registry: 9 EXTERNAL-only gov_v3_* parameters (4 calibratable, 5 fixed);
    179 targets / 126 eligible / 53 fixed; identity 81760179...
    
    revision5/exit_shadow.py: passive observer that exits every real fill under
    alternative policies on the engine's own per-bar inputs; the legacy policy must

    R5 diagnostics: governor trace tool for bay-restricted Stage A blocks
    
    scripts/r5_governor_trace.py reuses the Step 5 worker's sealed block loader and
    builds the engine as execute_block does, restricted to one bay's canonical
    symbols. Pass-through wrappers record the gain schedule (begin_bar environment,
    apply_runtime_profile), the outer realized-R PID, the entry comparator
    (dynamic_z, droop, overspeed limit), the inner per-position PID, the Mark V
    limiter, and bay protection and admission. --verify-passthrough reruns
    uninstrumented and requires an identical trade list. No engine, protocol,
    registry or Stage A state is modified.

commit c0b4672fa45498d628f1646d60c75fd206803755
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 10:54:25 +0000

    R5 governor: noise-scaled path-error tolerance (gov_path_error_sigma)
    
    Trial 0 under full authority (146 trades, PF 0.15) attributed the loss to
    GOVERNOR_PATH_ERROR: 82 exits, net -12.4k, PF 0.01, almost all within 1-3
    bars, while trades held 6-20 bars were profitable before costs. The inner
    loop exited once the trade lagged its reference path by max(|target_r|,
    |dynamic_offset_max|) = 0.30R -- the outer loop's realized-R setpoint reused
    as a tracking tolerance. One 1-minute bar moves ~0.8R (1R = 1.2 ATR), so that
    fired on noise.
    
    The tolerance is now gov_path_error_sigma * (ATR / initial risk) *
    sqrt(elapsed bars): the lag must exceed the market's own noise envelope.
    New registry parameter gov_path_error_sigma (EXTERNAL-only, calibratable,
    default 2.0 in [1.0, 3.5]); 170 targets / 122 eligible; new frozen identity.
    Without the noise inputs the governor keeps the legacy tolerance (native plant
    unchanged); the replay's position decision fails closed if ATR is unavailable.
    
    r5_loss_attribution.py also reads Step 5 candidate output (per-block trades).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 3de619f50c57c3bde8105a3d998f408d8b40abad
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 08:23:02 +0000

    R5 governor: overspeed limit for momentum entries and ranked FSRN
    
    Under full authority the governor admitted 0 of 3559 real candidates (block 1,
    trial 0). Two scale mismatches caused it:
    
    - The z comparator was a mean-reversion gate (BUY only when price is >= 1.9
      sigma below its mean) while PA candidates follow momentum. The governor now
      takes an entry_mode; the replay engine uses trend_overspeed, which admits
      unless the side-signed z exceeds -base_z + feedback offset - grid droop.
      Poor realized R and an adverse grid lower that limit, as they lower
      dynamic_z. mean_reversion remains the default for the native plant.
    - FSRN compared raw PA/studies confidence (candidates pass at >= 0.15,
      typically 0.15-0.4) with a 0.60 hurdle. FSRN is now the side-aligned min of
      each measure's causal percentile rank over gov_z_window_bars, so the hurdle
      means "top 40% of recent conviction". ID confidence (identical to PA
      confidence) is dropped. No registry change.
    
    Adds a regression test that a full-authority replay with the real decision
    path admits momentum candidates.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

    R5: fix exposure double count, wall-clock and fail-open fallbacks, exit bookkeeping order
    
    H2  ECS plant demand is now a total-loading setpoint (grid, protection, bay
        availability).  Current exposure is enforced once, by the paper admission
        cap (budget * reference - current exposure).  Previously the ECS also
        subtracted exposure headroom, so reachable gross exposure converged to
        ~55% of max_gross_exposure_fraction.  Headroom and the ClosedLoopSupervisor
        new-risk derate are still validated and reported as ECS reasons.
    H3  Pre-submit gates use the replay event time only; the datetime.now()
        fallback is removed.  An invalid replay timestamp now stops the run.
    H4  _in_trading_window fails closed (records TRADING_WINDOW_FAULT) and reads
        tz-aware timestamps on the exchange (Asia/Kolkata) clock.
    H5  _execute_exit updates the authoritative books (completed trades, symbol
        lockouts, equity, open_trades, exit state, MTM) before realized-R feedback
        and research telemetry, so a later defect can no longer leave a flat broker
        position recorded as open.  bars_held is never fabricated; without exit
        controller state the expectancy outcome is recorded as unavailable.
        CausalEntryExpectancyLedger.record_outcome validates the full outcome
        before consuming the pending candidate.

commit 4d90b5717f74a505847e7f1610e835ca180fec62
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-15 08:07:28 +0000

    Add Engine C: R5 CCPP engine executed natively by Backtrader
    
    engine_c/ drives the shared R5 decision code from completed Backtrader bars
    and sends approved intents as native Backtrader market orders to BackBroker.
    Fills happen at the next bar's open with independent NSE commission and
    slippage configuration. R5 books positions only from Backtrader execution
    bits. Native partial (FixedBarPerc), cancel, margin and venue-rule reject
    paths are handled. Working entries reserve concurrency, gross, sector and
    bay capacity. A FillLedger/Reconciler compares Backtrader accounting with
    the R5 fill-derived and trade ledgers after every event, every tick and at
    completion, and fails closed on a break.
    
    Adds the historical-data contract (manifest verification, raw-row audit),
    the CLI runner, an Engine A reference runner, a read-only three-engine
    comparison tool, a dependency manifest and 19 tests. Engine A and Engine B

commit 6ab7606d2d6e3dcacf3582789c56bdc1b95a7ed2
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-15 01:31:10 +0000

    Wire the native R5 five-bay plant into the PAPER_APPLY trading loop
    
    In PAPER_APPLY the orchestrator now drives CentralPlantMasterDCS directly:
    
    - Every bar: plant.step_bar() applies an R5 dynamic environment (bay
      governor/AVR/relay gains), steps the HRSG thermal cycle from GTG mass
      flow (volume ratio) x exhaust temperature (range/ATR), and rebalances
      capital so low steam pressure derates CSTG1/CSTG2/BPSTG. The snapshot's
      per-bay gain schedule scales the MPC entry/exit PIDs and the continuous
      exit PID.
    - Entry: evaluate_entry() gates every candidate (side-aware,
      trend_overspeed comparator); quantity = min(quantity, AVR lot capped by
      bay HRSG headroom x governor FSR).
    - Fill: on_trade_filled() consumes the Engine-A latch and binds the trade
      to its bay with its own governor inner loop; release_position() on close.
    - Positions: evaluate_position_control() every bar; substation/SEL/AVR
      trips, Engine-A 15:15 square-off and HRSG pressure collapse arm an exit
      at the next open as plant_trip:<reason>.
    
    Also fixes EngineStateStore(":memory:"), which opened a new empty database
    per connection so the Engine-A latch table never existed.
    
    scripts/r5_plant_wiring_probe.py runs the instrumented 100-bar replay.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UE4gousSZRwX4exwc8jWxK

commit 86a7fcaa433aa066eae08d3b342661d35bd50028
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-10-01 02:24:11 +0000

    docs(r5): black-box audit of the sealed V2 engine, with code evidence and a fix order
    
    Walks PA, chart studies, ID, MPC/PID, governor entry and position control, exit
    PID, sizing, risk/pre-submit gates and costs. Main findings: PA sums
    non-directional inputs into the signed signal; six confidence thresholds, of
    which the calibrated one never binds; exits decided by a ~uniform percentile-rank
    conviction gate that ignores minimum hold; PID outputs clamped, advisory or used
    as on/off triggers; Gate12 rejects ~1/3 of valid candidates by float rounding at
    rr == 1.5; HMM fed a gappy series; 1-minute-ATR stops make costs ~0.5R.
    
    The ID research hook now also records PA's four components and whether the
    directional terms alone give the same side, to test the PA-1 hypothesis on blade.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 2eeccdf9bfaee0954181486ea373c1da9f3c23aa
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    diag(r5): break-even sweep on synthesized fills; first-fill hold-to-close competitor
    
    - The friction sweep no longer re-uses recorded fills. Pre-slippage market
      prices are recovered once with the sealed 5 bps; at each of 0/1/2/3/4/5 bps

      executed entry per symbol and session, held to the session close. It is a
      lower bound on a first-raw-signal/EOD strategy, since it still waits for the

commit 87c0a8999c57a5e27d230b4eb411124667ad7a5b
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:41:29 +0000

    diag(r5): fix look-ahead in time-matched controls (use other sessions)
    
    The +/-30-bar same-session control window (cbfdaca) included the bars just
    before the entry. Every R5 entry follows a 0.6-2.5R run in its own direction,
    so controls placed there rode the move that triggered the entry: on the V2
    Stage-A run the control mean jumped to +0.45R at 15 bars (82% positive) and
    the reported entry "edge" to -0.36R. That was a biased null, not a finding.
    
    Controls are now drawn from the block's OTHER sessions: same symbol, side and
    risk unit, within +/-30 minutes of the trade's time of day, entered at the bar
    close, full horizon where that session allows (the session-close horizon runs
    to each control's own close). With no other session there is no control and
    the trade is excluded from the edge statistics. Regression test: a run before
    the entry on the same day must not appear in the controls.

commit f53c7f529af6a94fa75452afa72d742b4191254d
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-30 12:15:35 +0000

    diag(r5): measure the output as an exposure pulse train
    
    The whole R5 stack emits one thing per symbol: an exposure pulse (leading edge
    = entry and polarity, width = bars held, trailing edge = exit, off-interval =
    gap to the next pulse on the same symbol and session). Each pulse pays a
    switching loss (round-trip friction, R) and captures an energy (pre-slippage
    market move, R); energy - loss = net.
    
    Reported per source and pooled: pulse count, SELL share, width median/IQR and
    share <= 3 bars, pulses per active symbol-session, off-interval median and
    share <= 5/15 min, polarity flips within a session, and energy vs switching
    loss by width bucket (1-3, 4-10, 11-30, 31+ bars) -- the data needed to set a
    minimum on-time, a refractory period and a repetition limit.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    R5 diagnostics: governor trace tool for bay-restricted Stage A blocks
    
    scripts/r5_governor_trace.py reuses the Step 5 worker's sealed block loader and
    builds the engine as execute_block does, restricted to one bay's canonical
    symbols. Pass-through wrappers record the gain schedule (begin_bar environment,
    apply_runtime_profile), the outer realized-R PID, the entry comparator

commit c0b4672fa45498d628f1646d60c75fd206803755
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 10:54:25 +0000

    R5 governor: noise-scaled path-error tolerance (gov_path_error_sigma)
    
    Trial 0 under full authority (146 trades, PF 0.15) attributed the loss to
    GOVERNOR_PATH_ERROR: 82 exits, net -12.4k, PF 0.01, almost all within 1-3
    bars, while trades held 6-20 bars were profitable before costs. The inner
    loop exited once the trade lagged its reference path by max(|target_r|,
    |dynamic_offset_max|) = 0.30R -- the outer loop's realized-R setpoint reused
    as a tracking tolerance. One 1-minute bar moves ~0.8R (1R = 1.2 ATR), so that
    fired on noise.
    
    The tolerance is now gov_path_error_sigma * (ATR / initial risk) *
    sqrt(elapsed bars): the lag must exceed the market's own noise envelope.
    New registry parameter gov_path_error_sigma (EXTERNAL-only, calibratable,
    default 2.0 in [1.0, 3.5]); 170 targets / 122 eligible; new frozen identity.
    Without the noise inputs the governor keeps the legacy tolerance (native plant
    unchanged); the replay's position decision fails closed if ATR is unavailable.
    
    r5_loss_attribution.py also reads Step 5 candidate output (per-block trades).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JsmFWry8LbmGjYXciKhPoH

commit 3de619f50c57c3bde8105a3d998f408d8b40abad
Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
Date:   2026-09-28 08:23:02 +0000

    R5 governor: overspeed limit for momentum entries and ranked FSRN
    
    Under full authority the governor admitted 0 of 3559 real candidates (block 1,
    trial 0). Two scale mismatches caused it:
    
    - The z comparator was a mean-reversion gate (BUY only when price is >= 1.9
      sigma below its mean) while PA candidates follow momentum. The governor now
      takes an entry_mode; the replay engine uses trend_overspeed, which admits
      unless the side-signed z exceeds -base_z + feedback offset - grid droop.
      Poor realized R and an adverse grid lower that limit, as they lower
      dynamic_z. mean_reversion remains the default for the native plant.
    - FSRN compared raw PA/studies confidence (candidates pass at >= 0.15,
      typically 0.15-0.4) with a 0.60 hurdle. FSRN is now the side-aligned min of
      each measure's causal percentile rank over gov_z_window_bars, so the hurdle
      means "top 40% of recent conviction". ID confidence (identical to PA
      confidence) is dropped. No registry change.
    
    Adds a regression test that a full-authority replay with the real decision
    path admits momentum candidates.

    R5: fix exposure double count, wall-clock and fail-open fallbacks, exit bookkeeping order
    
    H2  ECS plant demand is now a total-loading setpoint (grid, protection, bay
        availability).  Current exposure is enforced once, by the paper admission
        cap (budget * reference - current exposure).  Previously the ECS also
        subtracted exposure headroom, so reachable gross exposure converged to
        ~55% of max_gross_exposure_fraction.  Headroom and the ClosedLoopSupervisor
        new-risk derate are still validated and reported as ECS reasons.
    H3  Pre-submit gates use the replay event time only; the datetime.now()
        fallback is removed.  An invalid replay timestamp now stops the run.
    H4  _in_trading_window fails closed (records TRADING_WINDOW_FAULT) and reads
        tz-aware timestamps on the exchange (Asia/Kolkata) clock.
    H5  _execute_exit updates the authoritative books (completed trades, symbol
        lockouts, equity, open_trades, exit state, MTM) before realized-R feedback
        and research telemetry, so a later defect can no longer leave a flat broker
        position recorded as open.  bars_held is never fabricated; without exit
        controller state the expectancy outcome is recorded as unavailable.
        CausalEntryExpectancyLedger.record_outcome validates the full outcome
        before consuming the pending candidate.

* 8f14713 Fix backtest determinism via stable regime random-state seed Real, confirmed bug affecting all external-engine backtests: the GaussianHMM regime classifier was initialized with random_state=hash(symbol) where hash() is Python's randomized string hash (different every process invocation unless PYTHONHASHSEED is pinned). Two consecutive runs of the identical 6-month INFY backtest against the same code produced different trade counts (179 vs 178 completed trades), proving the regime classifications changed run-to-run purely from the randomized seed. What changed: - determinism_guard.py: new shared module that pins BLAS/LAPACK threading   env vars for scripts. Sole purpose: be the first import in every   non-pytest entrypoint so BLAS/LAPACK single-threading applies before   any numpy use (env vars read at interpreter startup). Does NOT fix   the Python hash randomization bug (that must be fixed in source), but   documents why both guards are needed and prevents future env-var leaks. - regime_id_box.py: replace hash(symbol) with zlib.crc32(symbol.encode())   % (2**31), which is deterministic across runs and symbol-agnostic. Added   comment documenting the real bug class and the fix. - run_infy_6month_real.py: import determinism_guard as the very first   statement (before pandas, numpy, anything transitive). - diagnose_saturation_streaks_real_infy.py: same guard, same comment. Verification: two consecutive 6-month INFY runs with the fix applied now produce IDENTICAL results (187 trades, -39,093.23 net P&L, 445 id_approvals each time) -- determinism confirmed. Next session/commit will re-run saturation-exit diagnostics on these now-stable numbers to understand why saturation_exit_pa/studies fire zero times on this real window (streak counter analysis pending).
